title: Thyroid removal surgery
what: The surgeon removes all or half of the thyroid gland through a small cut low on the neck. The surgery is done under general anesthesia.
why: For nodules that may be cancer or for cancer, for a large goiter that presses on the neck, and for some forms of an overactive thyroid.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 3 hours; usually 1 to 3 days in the hospital
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
If your voice is important for work, for example if you are a singer, teacher, or announcer
If you had neck surgery before
If you or your relatives ever had problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood and hormone tests, a neck ultrasound, and an ECG. Often an ENT doctor checks your vocal cords before surgery.

prepare.title: Anesthesiologist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthesiologist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the evening before and no drinks for a few hours before. Your clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Things to pack
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes with a wide neckline, a phone charger, and the medicines you take every day.

bring: Your referral, test results, and ultrasound
Things for 1 to 3 days in the hospital
steps: On the day of surgery, you change clothes and an IV is put in a vein
In the operating room, the anesthesiologist gives the medicine and you fall asleep
The surgeon makes a small cut low on the neck, usually in a natural skin fold
All or part of the gland is removed, carefully protecting the voice nerves
The cut is stitched, sometimes with a thin drain tube
You wake up in the recovery room
feel: A sore throat when you swallow, from the breathing tube. It goes away in a few days
Your neck is sore and feels a bit tight. You will get pain medicine
Your voice may be hoarse or tire quickly. This is usually temporary
after: Your blood calcium level is usually checked
After the whole gland is removed, you take hormone pills every day for life. An endocrinologist sets the dose
Tissue test results usually take 1 to 2 weeks
Stitches are removed or dissolve on their own. Your surgeon will tell you which
red_flags: Your neck swells quickly, or it is hard to breathe or swallow: call emergency services right away
Tingling around your lips and in your fingers, or cramps in your hands: see a doctor urgently. It may be low calcium
A fever over 38 degrees, or redness or pus around the stitches

faq.q: Will I need hormone pills for life after surgery?
faq.a: If the whole gland was removed, yes, every day. If half was removed, not always. Often the remaining part can do the job on its own.

faq.q: Will my voice change after surgery?
faq.a: Most often the voice stays the same. Temporary hoarseness can happen and usually passes in a few weeks.
The cut is made in a neck fold. Over time, the scar usually becomes thin and pale.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Pack your things, your ID, and your list of medicines. Eat and drink only until the times your clinic gave you.
